keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Tyrol row). The page gives no area or boundary for the early county (the infobox 26,482 km2 is the later crown land with Trent and Brixen, undated); a 35 km circle at Meran (about 3,800 km2), soft. The page's 1004 and 1027 sentences give Trent and Bozen/Vinschgau to the Trent bishops and 1091 the Puster valley to the Brixen bishops, so the county was not the owner of all of the valleys.

correction.text: Tyrol in the sense of North and South Tyrol without the Lienz district, which belonged to Gorizia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1271 they divided their heritage and Meinhard became sole ruler of Tyrol'; he 'extended his Tyrolean lands down the Adige River to Salorno' and acquired 'territories in the Inn valley including the important salt mines around Hall' (both undated, in 1271-1295). The shape is Tirol (Austria) plus Bozen (Italy) minus a 30 km circle round East Tyrol (about 20,000 km2). Cliopatria's House of Habsburg row grows by 15.8 k km2 in 1363, and eu-09-a reads Tyrol as 16.8 k km2 in the Bavaria row: the shape is about a fifth too large, and Trent and Brixen are excluded. The page puts the Lienz district and the Puster valley with Gorizia until 1500 ('In 1500 he also acquired the remaining Gorizia territories around Lienz and the Puster Valley').

ledger.note: 1253: the counts of Gorizia take Tyrol. 'In 1253 Count Meinhard of Gorizia (Görz) inherited the Tyrolean lands...' Same state, new dynasty (Gorizia-Tyrol).

1271-1295: Meinhard II extends Tyrol. 'In 1271 they divided their heritage and Meinhard became sole ruler of Tyrol'; 'extended his Tyrolean lands down the Adige River to Salorno' and acquired 'territories in the Inn valley including the important salt mines around Hall'. The page gives no year for either acquisition (they lie in 1271-1295); 1271 is the start of his sole rule.

ledger.note: 10 February 1342: the Wittelsbachs take Tyrol. Margaret 'married Louis I of Brandenburg, Emperor Louis IV's eldest son, on 10 February 1342 in Meran'; he ruled Tyrol with her until his death in 1361 and Meinhard III followed. Same state, new dynasty; Cliopatria's Duchy of Bavaria row holds Tyrol in 1352-1362.

1363: Tyrol passes to the Habsburgs. 'Meinhard died without heirs less than two years later [after 1361]. Stephen II of Bavaria then invaded, and Margaret ceded Tyrol to Rudolf IV of Austria'; the county page: 'she bequeathed the county to Rudolph IV of Habsburg, Duke of Austria in 1363'.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages opened; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Tyrol row.

SCOPE. The dossier ends in 1363, when Tyrol became Habsburg land and Cliopatria's House of Habsburg row takes it (its area grows by 15.8 k km2 that year). The county itself continued as a crown land to 1919 (infobox 'Partitioned by Treaty of St Germain: September 10, 1919'; Trent and Brixen added 1803; Bavarian 1805-1814; Vorarlberg attached 1814); that later story belongs to house-of-habsburg / habsburg-monarchy. If the orchestrator wants Tyrol drawn as its own colour after 1363, extend this dossier: the gains of Kufstein, Kitzbuehel and Rattenberg (1504-1505, Landshut War, see duchy-of-bavaria) and of Lienz and the Puster valley (1500, page: 'In 1500 he also acquired the remaining Gorizia territories') are on opened pages but fall after 1363.

SHAPES. Tyrol 1271-1362 = Tirol (Austria) + Bozen (Italy) - a 30 km circle at 12.6E 46.85N (East Tyrol, Gorizia land to 1500), about 20 k km2 against 15.8-16.8 k in Cliopatria. Core 1140-1270 = a 35 km circle at Meran (11.16E 46.67N). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Meran' (place; Merano), 'Lienz', 'Brixen', 'Salorno'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The 1140 date is 'about'. (2) Meinhard II's valley gains are undated within 1271-1295. (3) The page does not date Meinhard's Trent/Brixen struggle. (4) Carinthia and Carniola: 'In 1286 he was enfeoffed with the Duchy of Carinthia and the adjacent March of Carniola'; the Carinthia dossier (eu-09) treats Carinthia as a separate state to 1335, so this is a personal union and is not a Tyrol gain (rule 4). (5) 1335: Louis gave Carinthia to Albert II of Austria; Margaret kept Tyrol; the extract does not say what else changed. (6) The 1342-1363 Wittelsbach period: eu-09-a's duchy-of-bavaria dossier keeps Tyrol inside the Bavarian outline (Cliopatria's 1352-1362 shape includes it) and flags it; Tyrol is drawn here as a separate state, so one of the two should take Tyrol out. (7) Margaret's bequest has no month on any opened page; the Habsburg takeover is dated 1363 only.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: county-of-gorizia (Lienz and the Puster valley), prince-bishopric-of-trent and prince-bishopric-of-brixen (Trent/Brixen were separate states to 1803).
